title: Differential Gene Expression in Halophyte Aeluropus littoralis
author: Fatemi, Hashemi-petroudi, et al.
materials: Total RNA from each stress treatment was isolated from about 100 mg of the frozen samples with the Trizol extraction kit (Invitrogen, USA) in three replications. Quality and quantity of isolated RNA were checked by agarose gel electrophoresis and spectrophotometer, respectively. The genomic DNA contamination was removed by DNase treatment (DNase I RNase-free, Thermo Scientific, USA). Root cells were lysed and mRNAs were isolated by capturing of poly(A+) RNA in streptavidin-coated tubes using a mRNA Capture kit (Roche, Switzerland). The first- and double-strand cDNA were synthesized by 5 μg of total RNA using a biotinylated oligo-dT primer in streptavidin-coated PCR tubes according to the manufacturer’s procedure. The restriction enzymes used for digestion of doubled strand cDNA were Taq I (Fermentase) and Mse I (Thermo Scientific, USA). The cDNA fragments released were purified and subsequently ligated to Taq I and Mse I. The pre-amplification reaction on ligation products was carried out using primers corresponding to Taq І (5′-GACGATGAGTCCTGACCGA-3′) and Mse I (5′-GACGATGAGTCCTGAG-3′) adapters. Twelve primer combinations were used for selective amplification; the primers were Mse І + 2: CC/CA/CT and Taq І + 2: GG/GC/AC/AT [18]. Selective amplification products (4 μl) were heat denatured and separated by electrophoresis in polyacrylamide gel (6%) containing 0.5X TBE. The gels were visualized by silver staining protocol and then were scanned by using imaging densitometer (GS-800, BioRad, USA).

Discrimination of gene expression patterns to ionic and osmotic effects was assayed based on the presence/absence (qualitative variants) of the visualized bands on gel electrophoresis. Gel profiles were quantified using Quantity One gel image analysis software (version 4.4.1, Bio-RAD, USA) resulted in measurement of band intensities per lane for each time interval. The interested bands were marked and cut from the dried gels. The excised bands were eluted in 50 μl double distilled sterile water at 95 °C for 15 min then hydrated overnight at 4 °C. The eluted TDFs were reamplified by using the same set of selective primers under the PCR conditions as mentioned for AFLP. The PCR products were then checked on 0.5 x TBE 1.5% agarose gel. After confirming the size of the bands, the PCR products were ligated into the pTZ57R/T T/A cloning vector (InsTAclone PCR Cloning Kit, Thermo Scientific, USA), and were directly electro-transformed into DH5 competent E.coli cells. Colony PCR was done with M13 F/R primers and after confirming the size of the band, they were sent for sequencing (GATC, Germany).

steps.title: Sterilize seeds and initiate culture
steps.instruction: Uncoat seeds, sterilize 1 min in 75 % ethanol, then 15 min in 2.5 % commercial bleach, rinse three times with sterile distilled water, and place seeds in a flask containing 50 ml full‑strength liquid MS medium supplemented with 3 % sucrose and vitamins; adjust medium pH to 5.8.

steps.title: Incubate initial plantlets
steps.instruction: Grow the seeded flasks in a growth chamber at 25 °C in darkness with constant shaking at 120 rpm for seven days.

steps.title: Subculture and add stress agents
steps.instruction: Transfer seven‑day‑old plantlets to fresh 50 ml liquid MS medium (same composition as above) and add NaCl or KCl at 200 mM and 400 mM, and PEG 6000 at 280 g L⁻¹ and 406 g L⁻¹ to obtain iso‑osmotic pressures of –0.9 MPa and –1.4 MPa, respectively, calculated with π = i c R T (R = 8.314472 L·kPa·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹) and converting bar to MPa.

steps.title: Incubate stressed plantlets
steps.instruction: Continue culturing the stressed plantlets for 14 days under the same chamber conditions (25 °C, darkness, 120 rpm).

steps.title: Harvest and store plant material
steps.instruction: After 14 days, measure whole‑plant fresh weight, quickly freeze the plants in liquid nitrogen, and store at –80 °C for downstream cDNA‑AFLP analysis.

steps.title: Experimental design and data analysis
steps.instruction: Arrange the experiment as a completely randomized design with five replications; analyse fresh‑weight data by ANOVA, assess significant differences with Duncan’s multiple range test (p < 0.05) using SPSS 16 software.

steps.title: Extract total RNA
steps.instruction: Grind ~100 mg of frozen plant tissue and isolate total RNA with the Trizol extraction kit (Invitrogen, USA) in three replicates; assess RNA quality by agarose‑gel electrophoresis and quantity by spectrophotometry.

steps.title: Remove genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Treat the RNA samples with DNase I RNase‑free (Thermo Scientific, USA) to eliminate genomic DNA contamination.

steps.title: Capture poly(A)+ mRNA
steps.instruction: Lyse root cells and isolate poly‑A⁺ RNA using streptavidin‑coated tubes and the mRNA Capture kit (Roche, Switzerland).

steps.title: Synthesize first‑ and double‑strand cDNA
steps.instruction: Use 5 µg of total RNA and a biotinylated oligo‑dT primer in streptavidin‑coated PCR tubes, following the manufacturer’s protocol, to generate first‑ and double‑strand cDNA.

steps.title: Digest cDNA with restriction enzymes
steps.instruction: Digest the double‑strand cDNA with Taq I (Fermentase) and Mse I (Thermo Scientific, USA).

steps.title: Purify and ligate adapters
steps.instruction: Purify the restriction fragments and ligate adapters compatible with Taq I and Mse I ends.

steps.title: Pre‑amplify ligation products
steps.instruction: Perform a pre‑amplification PCR using primers matching the Taq I adapter (5′‑GACGATGAGTCCTGACCGA‑3′) and the Mse I adapter (5′‑GACGATGAGTCCTGAG‑3′).

steps.title: Selective amplification of fragments
steps.instruction: Carry out selective amplification with twelve primer combinations (Mse I + 2: CC, CA, CT; Taq I + 2: GG, GC, AC, AT); take 4 µl of each product, heat‑denature, and resolve on a 6 % polyacrylamide gel containing 0.5 × TBE.

steps.title: Stain and image gels
steps.instruction: Silver‑stain the polyacrylamide gels, then scan the gels with a GS‑800 imaging densitometer (BioRad, USA).

steps.title: Select and excise bands
steps.instruction: Identify bands of interest, mark them, and cut the corresponding fragments from the dried gels.

steps.title: Elute DNA from gel pieces
steps.instruction: Elute each excised band in 50 µl double‑distilled sterile water at 95 °C for 15 min, then incubate overnight at 4 °C to hydrate.

steps.title: Re‑amplify eluted TDFs
steps.instruction: Re‑amplify the eluted fragments by PCR using the same selective primer combinations and cycling conditions as the AFLP selective amplification.

steps.title: Verify re‑amplified products
steps.instruction: Run the PCR products on a 0.5 × TBE 1.5 % agarose gel to confirm fragment size.

steps.title: Clone TDFs into vector
steps.instruction: Ligate the verified PCR products into the pTZ57R/T T/A cloning vector (InsTAclone PCR Cloning Kit, Thermo Scientific, USA).

steps.title: Transform E.coli and select colonies
steps.instruction: Electro‑transform the ligation mixture into DH5α competent E. coli cells, plate on selective media, and incubate.

steps.title: Screen colonies by PCR
steps.instruction: Perform colony PCR on transformants using M13 F and M13 R primers; confirm insert size by agarose‑gel electrophoresis.

steps.title: Sequence confirmed clones
steps.instruction: Send plasmids with correctly sized inserts to GATC (Germany) for Sanger sequencing.

steps.title: Perform bioinformatics analysis
steps.instruction: Trim vector and adapter sequences with VecScreen (NCBI); translate and BLASTX/BLASTN/TBLASTX against GenBank nr; annotate functions using Gene Ontology and UniProt; deposit 69 TDF sequences in GenBank dbEST (BioSample SAMN01924517, library LIBEST_028119, accession JZ191042–JZ191110); predict protein subcellular localization by BLASTX to Setaria italica followed by Plant‑PLoc analysis.
